title: News Corp chases regional audiences with AI-led stories
full_text:
The Herald Sun has outsourced coverage of local news to artificial intelligence, expanding its use of the technology from traffic and weather reports to generate articles for regional and community audiences without hiring more journalists.
Six years after shutting down dozens of print and digital titles serving those communities, the News Corp-owned masthead has published a handful of stories this week under the byline of 'Leader', the name of its newspaper group serving community news for the state. At the end of the articles, it flags those pieces were produced using AI.
The articles in The Herald Sun appear to draw on information from recent council meetings across several Melbourne metropolitan and regional areas including Moonee Valley, Monash City Council and others, and appear to be produced using minutes from those meetings, which are published online.
News Corp shuttered the 20 print titles under the Leader group banner in 2020 and has made a number of journalists in its local news division redundant since. It continues to publish content online under the digital banners of some of those titles.
The AI-generated articles note at the bottom that they form part of a News Corp ambition to "publish more regional and community stories than ever before". News Corp also states the articles were created with "AI assistance" and then edited and approved by an editor.
The publisher signed a global deal with ChatGPT-creator OpenAI worth $250 million in 2024, allowing the AI firm to use News Corp content in its responses.
This year, News Corp also signed a content licensing deal with Facebook-owner Meta worth US$50 million ($70 million) per year.
News Corp unveiled NewsGPT in 2025, allowing journalists to draft stories or summarise documents or meetings.
Australian media bosses, including local News Corp boss Michael Miller, have been vocal on lobbying the federal government for legislation requiring AI firms to compensate news outlets for the use of their content to train their language models and reproduce information.
During a National Press Club appearance two years ago, Miller said media companies should start using AI as a tool to produce better work, but insisted "we're not going to see journalists replaced by AI".
Many news organisations use AI in some, often limited ways in the production of news. However, most, including this masthead, forbid its use to write stories for publication or produce imagery or illustrations to accompany stories.
News Corp discontinued print publication of most of its regional titles in June 2020.
Reduced funding for local and regional news outlets has often left regional areas without any local news coverage aside from regional ABC bureaus. Nine, owner of this masthead, sold 160 regional titles to Australian Community Media in 2019, many of which have since been shuttered or made digital-only.
A spokesperson for the media union, the Media, Entertainment and Arts Alliance, said AI may help with efficiencies, but "it cannot replace the reporting, fact-checking and community knowledge that underpin trusted journalism".
